blocks.text: The United States incarcerates at a rate 5-10x higher than comparable democratic nations. This is not a natural response to crime -- it is the result of specific policy decisions made from the 1970s onward. Understanding mass incarceration requires separating the causes (policy choices), the mechanisms (drug war + mandatory minimums + sentencing guidelines), and the consequences (individual, family, community, fiscal).

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               US INCARCERATION LANDSCAPE                         |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  SCALE (2023 approx):                                            |
|  ~2 million incarcerated (jail + prison)                         |
|  ~1 in 100 adults                                                |
|  Rate: ~600 per 100,000 (Japan: 40; Germany: 70; UK: 130)        |
|                                                                  |
|  SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE:                                            |
|  Federal prisons:     BOP, 10% of population                     |
|  State prisons:       90% of population                          |
|  Local jails:         pretrial detention + short sentences        |
|  Immigration det.:    ICE detention (separate system)            |
|                                                                  |
|  RACIAL COMPOSITION:                                             |
|  Black Americans: 13% of US population, ~38% of prison pop.      |
|  Black men: 1 in 3 will be incarcerated in their lifetime        |
|  (vs. 1 in 17 for white men)                                     |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

FEDERAL PRISON POPULATION BY OFFENSE:
  ======================================
  Drug offenses: ~44% of federal inmates
  Weapons: ~17%
  Immigration: ~11%
  Property: ~6%
  Violent: ~7%

  STATE PRISON POPULATION BY OFFENSE:
  =====================================
  Violent: ~55% of state inmates
  Property: ~18%
  Drug: ~15%
  Other: ~12%

  KEY DISTINCTION:
  Federal prison = mostly drug/guns/immigration
  State prison = more violent, property

  JAIL (unconvicted):
  ~70% of jail inmates are PRETRIAL -- not convicted.
  Held because cannot afford bail.
  Bail amount: $10,000 median --> $1,000 bail bond fee
  Working class person spends weeks/months in jail
  awaiting trial, loses job, housing, family contact.
